evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The value is a plain YYYY-MM-DD date with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/3 {"dueDate":"2026-09-01"} returned 200 with the new date. PATCH /todos/2 {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null, so the date was removed. PATCH of the title only left the dueDate unchanged.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate 2026-02-30, 15.10.2026 and 2026-10-15T10:00:00 each returned 400. POST with numeric dueDate 123 returned 400. PATCH with 2026-02-30 and "bad" returned 400. But PATCH /todos/1 with {"dueDate":5} returned HTTP 500 with an InvalidOperationException stack trace instead of 400. A wrong-format value is therefore not always rejected with 400.
evidence.AC4: Test data, today = 2026-10-15: past (2026-10-01, open), future (null after patch), nodue (2026-09-01 after patch), today (2026-10-15, open), pastdone (2026-10-01, done). GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past todo (id 1) and the todo patched to 2026-09-01 (id 3). The todo due today, the todo without a due date and the done todo with a past date were excluded.
evidence.AC5: The list page at / showed each due date next to its todo, for example past2 2026-10-01, nodue 2026-09-01, today 2026-10-15 and pastdone 2026-10-01. The todo with no due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: On the list page, "überfällig" appeared only on past2 (2026-10-01) and nodue (2026-09-01). The todo due today, the todo without a due date and the done todo with a past date had no marker.
evidence.AC7: The page has a button "nur überfällige". Clicking it reduced the list from 5 todos to the 2 overdue ones, past2 and nodue.
